Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the sideswipe collision
you reported in Houston, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give the facts of what happened, if that's alright. I'm not comfortable giving my full name on tape right
now.
Q: That's acceptable for now. Can you describe where you were driving and what you were doing when the collision
occurred?
A: I was on the freeway in the right-hand lane, heading toward the downtown exit. Traffic was moderate. I signaled
and started moving left into the middle lane because my exit was coming up.
Q: Did you check your mirrors and blind spot before moving over?
A: I checked the mirror, and I thought the lane was clear. Then I felt a bump on the side of my car and heard scraping.
The other vehicle was already alongside me.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the contact?
A: Not clearly. It may have been in my blind spot. I didn't see it until the impact.
Q: Where did you feel the impact on your vehicle?
A: On the front passenger side, near the wheel well and the door.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My neck snapped forwrad and then back. The next morning I had stiffness and pain in my neck and upper
back, and I've had headaches since. I've been seeing a doctor for it.
Q: Did you seek medical care on the day of the collision?
A: I was checked at the scene and then went home. I went to a clinic two days later when the pain got worse.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I've been trying to keep working while dealing with this, and it's been hard.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
